arena_name: Case 6: ddos recon firewall evasion SOC Investigation
mission_prompt: Investigate the APT enterprise intrusion in D:\Security-logs-test\attack-cases-benchmark\case-6-ddos-recon-firewall-evasion\raw-logs. Reconstruct the full attack kill chain across authentication logs, process executions, and network flows. Extract all C2 indicators of compromise (IOCs), map MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and generate automated containment policies.

units.description: Read all files under the specified raw‑logs directory, parse authentication events, process execution records, and network flow entries into structured tables (CSV or JSON). Handle common log formats such as Windows Event Log XML, Sysmon CSV, and NetFlow logs.

Using the parsed datasets, identify sequential stages of the intrusion (Reconnaissance, Initial Access, Execution, Persistence, Command & Control, Impact). Correlate timestamps across logs to build a timeline and highlight key events such as credential dumping, lateral movement, or DDoS initiation.

From the kill‑chain data, pull out all unique IP addresses, domain names, URLs, file hashes, and registry keys that appear to be used for command & control or lateral movement. Deduplicate and annotate each IOC with its source log type.

units.task_name: Map IOCs to MITRE ATT&CK Techniques
units.description: For each IOC and kill‑chain event, map the activity to the most appropriate MITRE ATT&CK technique(s) (e.g., T1078 for Valid Accounts, T1040 for Network Sniffing). Generate a mapping table that includes technique ID, name, description, and evidence reference.

Using the IOC list and MITRE mapping, produce a set of containment rules suitable for common security tools (e.g., firewall ACLs, endpoint EDR policies, SIEM alerting). Include rule syntax examples for iptables/Windows Firewall, Suricata signatures, and Splunk queries.

We break the work into distinct phases: ingest & parse logs, identify kill‑chain events, extract IOCs, map MITRE techniques, and produce containment rules. Each phase depends on the previous one for accurate data flow.
